Who We Are We support the people who are changing education in Africa Injini EdTech Acceleration NPC is a registered Non-Profit Company (2017/193849/08) and Public Benefit Organisation based in Cape Town, South Africa with the purpose of improving educational outcomes in sub-Saharan Africa. Founded in 2017, Injini remains the only EdTech specialised accelerator in Africa. Injini was established on the belief that innovation and technology - developed by Africa, for Africa - can help solve the continent’s most pressing education challenges. What EdTech Founders Learn When Ideal Assumptions Meet Real-World Friction What We Do Programs & Projects EdTech Acceleration Ecosystem Development AI for Education New EdTech Week 2026 EdTech for Employment New Other Projects Ecosystem Development Knowledge & Insights Research & Insights Resource Hub EdTech Map Blog Ecosystem Development About the EdTech Accelerator SA EdTech Week Explore the Resource Hub Ecosystem Development SA EdTech Week About Injini Our Portfolio Support Our Impact Let's Chat Let's Chat All Posts What EdTech Founders Learn When Ideal Assumptions Meet Real-World Friction Written by: Injini Published on: September 2, 2026 EdTech founders tend to build for an idealised user: a fast connection, a modern device, and someone who already knows their way around a browser. Real classrooms rarely match that picture. To find out where the gap actually sits, we watched real users test EdTech products on their own entry-level mobile devices, in field studies across Kenya, South Africa, and Rwanda. We found that an EdTech product can look good on a fully charged demo laptop, but real-world deployment tells a radically different story. In our observations, up to 75% of participants struggled with foundational web mechanics, such as multi-tab navigation or copy-pasting text, before ever interacting with the instructional material.
